data.name: Chitaranjan
data.gender_notes: Chitaranjan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Chitaranjan is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Chit' meaning mind and 'Ranjan' meaning to please. This name signifies one who pleases the mind or one who is a source of joy and happiness to the mind. The name Chitaranjan carries the meaning “One who pleases the mind” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chitaranjan usually hope their child will grow to embody one who pleases the mind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Chitaranjan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “One who pleases the mind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chitaranjan total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_sanskrit.name: चितरान्जन
in_sanskrit.meaning: Moon with beautiful marks or spots
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: चित्र (Chitra) meaning 'beautiful', आ (Aa) meaning 'with', र (Ra) meaning 'moon', आ (An) meaning 'with', ज (Ja) meaning 'beautiful marks' or 'spots', न (Na) meaning 'new', and ज (Ja) meaning 'born'. So, Chitaranjan means 'Newborn moon with beautiful marks or spots'.

in_hindi.name: चितरान्जन
in_hindi.meaning: चित्र (Chitra) + आ (Aa) + र (Ra) + आ (An) + ज (Ja) + न (Na) + ज (Ja)
in_hindi.long_meaning: This name is derived from Sanskrit. 'चित्र (Chitra)' means 'beautiful', 'आ (Aa)' means 'with', 'र (Ra)' means 'moon', 'आ (An)' means 'with', 'ज (Ja)' means 'beautiful marks' or 'spots', 'न (Na)' means 'new', and 'ज (Ja)' means 'born'. So, Chitaranjan means 'Newborn moon with beautiful marks or spots'.

in_tamil.name: சித்தராஜன
in_tamil.long_meaning: This name is derived from Sanskrit and transliterated to Tamil. 'சித்தர் (Chitrar)' means 'beautiful' or 'decorated', 'ா (Aa)' is a vowel sound, 'ஜலம் (Jalam)' means 'moon', 'பரிவை (Parivai)' means 'marks' or 'spots', and 'சிவன் (Civan)' is a term for God. So, Chitaranjan can be interpreted as 'Beautiful moon with divine marks or spots'.

in_telugu.name: చితరాజన

data.cultural_impact: The name Chitaranjan holds a deep cultural significance in Hinduism, as it is associated with the legend of Lord Krishna. In one popular story, Lord Krishna was once called Chitrakootananda or Chitra Koota Raja, meaning the Lord of Chitrakoot (the forest of beautiful images). This is where he spent some time with his divine lover Radha, also referred to as Rani (Queen) in various depictions. The name Chitaranjan can be seen as a reflection of this cultural legacy, representing one who brings joy and pleasure to the mind, much like Lord Krishna.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Chitaranjan signifies the pursuit of inner joy and peace. It implies one who is striving to keep their mind serene and focused, to please it with pure thoughts, actions, and experiences. In yoga and meditation practices, the mind is often referred to as the 'Chitta,' and the aim is to 'Ranjana' or please it, through the practice of Dhyana (meditation). As such, the name Chitaranjan serves as a constant reminder to keep the mind joyful and content.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Chitaranjan: Radiant heart, filled with joy and compassion. The name evokes a sense of inner light, purity, and divine grace. The one who carries this name is believed to radiate happiness and kindness, inspiring peace and harmony around them.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Chitraranjana was a king of the Vatsa kingdom in the 5th century BCE. The name Chitaranjan carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
